exposure: Gestational age at elective cesarean section (37 weeks, 38 weeks, 39 weeks)
cohort: The study included 435 women with two or more prior cesarean deliveries, analyzed based on their gestational age at elective cesarean section.
finding: The optimal timing for elective cesarean sections in women with two or more prior cesareans is 39 weeks of gestation, associated with the best neonatal outcomes, including lower NICU admission rates and healthy birth weights.
mod_finding: Elective cesarean sections constituted 81.0% of the procedures, with no significant difference in the distribution of elective versus emergency cesareans across the studied gestational weeks.
birth_weight: N/A (not specified as an inclusion criterion, but 'healthy birth weights' was an outcome finding)
gest_age: The study investigated outcomes across gestational ages of 37 weeks, 38 weeks, and 39 weeks at delivery.
